author: Traditionally Moses
authorNote: Jewish and Christian tradition names Moses. Many modern scholars think the five books of the Law were drawn together from several sources over centuries, reaching their final form around the 6th–5th century BC; others defend substantial Mosaic authorship.
date: Traditionally c. 1400s BC; final form debated (see Genesis)
overview: Abraham's descendants have become slaves in Egypt, and God calls Moses to lead them out. After the plagues and the Passover, God rescues Israel through the sea and meets them at Mount Sinai. There he gives the Ten Commandments, makes a covenant with them, and has them build the tabernacle so he can live among his people.
storyPlace: The founding rescue story of Israel. Later writers, and the New Testament, look back to the Exodus and Passover again and again.
